chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Mistaken credit for Joe Thomas's song in a film
summary: Shapiro-Bernstein thought a song used by Glenn Miller and Artie Shaw was McRae's, but it belonged to the other tenor player named Joe Thomas.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: Did you ever have any songs performed on film?

No. Not -- he called me one day and thought they had 'Back Bay Shuffle' or one of the things (inaudible) Glen Gray had did, but it wasn't mine. It was the other tenor player. Remember the tenor player who had the band with Louie before I took the band over? I think his name was Joe Thomas, too. He wrote this big thing. Artie Shaw did one of his big songs. Glenn Miller did one of the things. And they called me -- I think Shapiro-Bernstein had the song. And they called me up -- they
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
thought it mine -- (inaudible) they had in the picture, but it wasn't mine. It was the other tenor player with Louie.
They say, "The tenor player with Louie" -- they didn't know who (inaudible). He say, "Well, you know, what's the tenor player with Louie Armstrong?"
So Shapiro-Bernstein thought -- well Elliott and I were very close friends, another big publishing company.
He called me and say, "I think your picture -- Glenn Miller did you song."
I say, "No, that's not mine. You mean the other tenor player, Joe Thomas," you know. The other Thomas, you know.
I say, "No, that was his song." Because Artie Shaw did the song, too. Did the instrumental. It was a big instrumental.
